title: Sales Enablement: Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Decks, Pricing Guidance, Case Studies, Security FAQ
author: Maya Thompson
content:
Overview

This document is the canonical sales enablement playbook for Redwood Inference covering: positioning and messaging, competitive briefs, a repeatable pitch-deck framework, pricing guidance for prospects, two representative case studies, and a prospect-facing security FAQ. Use this as the single source of truth for sales and solutions engineering (SE) conversations.

Owners & audience
- Primary owners: GTM Enablement (Maya Thompson), Product Marketing (Diego Alvarez), Solutions Engineering (Liam Chen)
- Audience: AEs, SDRs, SEs, Customer Success, Channel Partners
- Review cadence: Quarterly or on major product/price changes

1) Positioning & Top-Level Messaging

Quick pitch (30–60s):
- Redwood Inference: the developer-first inference platform that makes production LLMs predictable, performant, and cost-effective across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Three core value props (one-liners):
1. Production performance: predictable latency and throughput through a GPU-optimized serving runtime and smart routing.
2. Cost controls: batching, KV caching, and quantization recommendations that reduce per-token unit economics without degrading quality.
3. Deployment flexibility & security: same API and tooling across hosted, dedicated, and private (VPC / on-prem) with enterprise-grade controls.

Evidence & supporting bullets (use in discovery):
- Benchmarks: p99 latency targets: hosted API (<= 200ms for gen-64), dedicated with reserved capacity (<= 120ms), private depends on infra config.
- Cost wins: typical 25–45% token-cost reduction on conversational workloads when applying Redwood Optimize recommendations (customer-supplied workloads).
- Reliability: multi-tier routing and model fallbacks with SLA-backed Dedicated offerings.

Use-case framing (pick the best fit):
- Assistants & chat experiences (low-latency LLM responses)
- Document search & L2 retrieval (embeddings + reranking pipeline)
- Productionization of LLM features for regulated data (Private deployment + KMS/HSM)

2) Competitive Briefs (how to win deals)

Competitors covered: Major cloud providers (managed endpoints), LLM API vendors, inference runtime vendors.

Competitive matrix (summary):
| Dimension | Redwood Inference | Managed Cloud Endpoints | LLM API Vendor X | Self-host Runtime Y |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Performance (low-latency) | Strong (runtime + routing) | Medium | Varies | Strong (ops burden) |
| Cost optimization tools | Built-in (Optimize) | Limited | Minimal | Custom / manual |
| Deployment modes | Hosted / Dedicated / Private | Hosted / Cloud-only | Hosted | Self-host only |
| Enterprise controls & compliance | Audit logs, KMS, VPC options | Good (cloud controls) | Limited | Depends on customer |
| Time to value | Fast (API + quickstarts) | Fast | Fast | Slow (ops) |

Tactical rebuttals (short answers for objection handling):
- "We already use cloud provider endpoints": Redwood provides consistent unit economics, built-in optimizer tooling, and private deployment options—reducing long-term cost and ops overhead for multi-model fleets.
- "We want on-prem": We offer Private with on-prem packaging and an SRE-run bundle for initial deployment; PM/SE will provide architecture + runbook.
- "Vendor lock-in concerns": Same API across hosted/dedicated/private; exportable model configs and KV-cache metadata.

3) Pitch Deck Framework (recommended slide flow)

Use a 10–12 slide deck for initial meetings:
1. Title + one-line value prop
2. Customer pain (3 bullets)
3. Redwood solution overview (1-slide architecture diagram)
4. Key differentiators (3 bullets)
5. Performance & cost evidence (benchmarks + testimonial)
6. Deployment options (hosted/dedicated/private)
7. Security & compliance highlights
8. Pricing overview & commercial model
9. Case study 1 (summary metrics)
10. Next steps & trial offer

Pitch tips for SEs:
- Tailor the performance slide with region/hardware notes when discussing Dedicated/Private.
- Use our benchmarking numbers only when you have the same model/sequence-length assumptions; reference the benchmark doc (link in related_pages).
- For enterprise prospects, bring the security FAQ slide to the first demo.

4) Pricing Guidance (discovery checklist & indicative pricing)

Discovery checklist (what SE should gather):
- Target QPS/throughput and expected percent p99 SLA requirement
- Typical request size (tokens/input length) and prompt/response distribution
- Model family(s) and whether they need custom weights or open models
- Data residency and compliance requirements
- Expected monthly token and embedding volume

Indicative commercial models (high level, for initial conversations):
- Hosted API: usage-based (per-token generation & embedding unit) with volume bands and soft quotas.
- Dedicated: monthly reserved GPU capacity + overage rates and burst credits.
- Private: platform license + deployment & support fee; annual contracts typical for enterprise.

Sample pricing table (indicative only — use legal quoting tool for official numbers):
| Offer | Unit | Indicative list price (USD) | Typical customers |
| Hosted (gen) | per 1k generated tokens | $0.60 | Startups / dev POCs |
| Hosted (embeddings) | per 1k embeddings | $0.40 | Search / retrieval apps |
| Dedicated (reserved GPU) | per GPU / month | $5,000 - $15,000 | Mid-market to Enterprise |
| Private | platform + support | Custom (license + services) | Regulated enterprises |

Discounting guidance:
- Discount bands tied to committed monthly usage or 12/24 month reserved capacity contracts.
- SEs: do not promise non-standard commercial terms; route requests for exceptions to Sales Operations.

5) Case Studies (two short win stories to reference)

Case study: FinTech assistant (mid-market)
- Problem: Customer needed low-latency, auditable conversational assistant for internal ops with PII controls.
- Solution: Dedicated deployment with VPC networking, KMS-integrated encryption, and Canary rollout to 200 users.
- Outcome: Reduced average response time from 650ms to 110ms and lowered token costs by 32% after applying Redwood Optimize recommendations.
- References: SE lead (Priya Nair), internal playbook / contact.

Case study: E-commerce search ranking (startup)
- Problem: Poor search relevance and high infra cost from multiple model calls.
- Solution: Hybrid pipeline (embeddings + reranker) on Hosted API with KV prefix caching for repeated queries.
- Outcome: 18% uplift in conversion for search-originated sessions and 28% reduction in per-query cost.

6) Security FAQ for Prospects (short answers for the most common questions)

Q: Where is my data stored?
A: For Hosted API, data is stored in our audited cloud regions; customers can choose region. For Dedicated and Private, data remains in customer-controlled VPC or on-prem environment.

Q: How do you handle encryption and keys?
A: Data at-rest and in-transit is encrypted (TLS1.3). We support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations for Dedicated and Private.

Q: Do you retain prompts or training data?
A: By default, Redwood does not use customer prompts or responses to train models. Retention policies can be configured; we support contract language for stricter non-retention.

Q: What compliance certifications do you have?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and is pursuing ISO 27001. Specific compliance evidence is available through the security pack for qualified enterprise prospects.

Q: How do you support data residency requirements?
A: We deploy region-specific hosted endpoints and offer Dedicated/Private deployments to satisfy strict residency needs.

Q: Incident notification & audit logging?
A: Dedicated and Private options provide extended audit logging and webhook-based incident notifications. Our incident-response process aligns with the security-and-compliance incident_response_security playbook.

7) Playbook: How to run a 30-day trial (SE checklist)

Preparation (days -7 to 0):
1. Collect discovery checklist answers and select trial model(s).
2. Confirm region, expected traffic profile, and data residency needs.
3. Provision trial keys or temporary Dedicated capacity; set up Prometheus/trace hooks if requested.

Trial execution (days 0–21):
- Day 0–3: Onboard, run baseline benchmarks with customer data (sanitized), capture p50/p95/p99 latencies.
- Day 4–14: Apply Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching, caching, quantization), measure cost & quality delta on a shared evaluation prompt set.
- Day 14–21: Iterate on prompt engineering and reranking thresholds; prepare performance summary.

Close / handoff (days 22–30):
- Present results with metrics (latency, cost delta, quality metrics).
- Provide recommended commercial path (Hosted volume vs Dedicated vs Private).
- Handoff to Sales Ops for formal quote and to Customer Success for onboarding if contract signed.
